title: 5 Tips for a GMAT Study Plan While Working Full-Time
description: Most GMAT advice assumes hours of free time and still describes the old test. Here are 5 realistic tips for preparing for the GMAT Focus Edition around a full-time job, with a sample week.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: Most GMAT study guides are written for people with unlimited free time: wake at 6, study for four hours, take a break, study for three more. That isn't a plan for someone with a job. A lot of them also describe a test that no longer exists. Since early 2024 the only version you can book is the GMAT Focus Edition, which dropped Sentence Correction, the essay and geometry, and added a Data Insights section. Here's a plan built around the hours you actually have, for the exam you'll actually sit.

content.heading: Know the exam you're preparing for
content.body: Three sections of 45 minutes each, 64 questions in all, 2 hours and 15 minutes plus one optional 10-minute break, scored from 205 to 805. You choose the order of the sections, and you can bookmark questions and change up to three answers per section before time runs out, according to GMAC, which runs the exam:

table.caption: GMAT Focus Edition, section by section
rows: Arithmetic and algebra problem solving, with no calculator
Data sufficiency and reading tables, graphs and multi-source data, with an on-screen calculator

content.heading: 1. Use your commute for review, not new material
list: A 30 to 60 minute commute, twice a day, is real time, but it's poor time for new problem solving
Use it for low-effort review: go through your error log, reread the explanations for Critical Reasoning questions you missed, or revisit the logic of a Data Sufficiency question that tripped you
Vocabulary flashcards, a staple of older GMAT advice, are low value now. Sentence Correction is gone, and Verbal rewards following an argument, not knowing rare words

content.heading: 2. One good hour beats three tired ones
list: After a full workday you aren't at your sharpest, so don't schedule your hardest section for 10 pm
Pick one consistent hour, ideally soon after work before you're fully drained, and protect it
Rotate the three sections through the week rather than drilling one. Each counts equally towards your score, and Data Insights is the one older prep books don't cover at all

content.heading: 3. Let weekends carry the timed practice
list: Weekday hours are for maintenance and targeted review. Weekends are for full 45-minute timed sections and, every second or third weekend, a full practice exam
Practise in the section order you plan to use on test day, since you get to choose it, and get used to pacing at about two minutes a question
Practise using bookmarks and the three edits per section. Knowing when to flag a question and move on is a skill, and you don't want to learn it in the real exam

content.heading: 4. Track focused time, not just days studied
list: "Did I study today" hides how little some days actually were
Track focused minutes per section. A week of 4 hours on Quant and 20 minutes on Data Insights looks fine as a yes/no checklist and terrible as numbers
Look at the totals each Sunday and move next week's hours towards the weakest section

content.heading: 5. Take one full day off every week
list: It's the first thing people cut when time is tight, and the one that costs the most later
Studying every day on top of a full-time job is a fast route to quitting around week four
One genuine day off keeps a plan of two to three months sustainable

content.heading: A sample week
content.body: About 6 to 7 hours a week, which over 10 to 12 weeks adds up to a realistic total for many working candidates. Adjust the blocks to your own weakest section:

table.caption: A sample GMAT Focus week around a full-time job
rows: 1 hour: Quant problem set, then review every miss
1 hour: Verbal, a Critical Reasoning set plus one reading passage
1 hour: Data Insights set, with the calculator, as on test day
45 minutes: error log review across all three sections
Off, or a light commute review
2 to 3 hours: two timed 45-minute sections in your test-day order, then review
Off. Every second or third week, swap Saturday for a full practice exam

content.heading: Common mistakes
list: Preparing from a pre-2024 book or course full of Sentence Correction, geometry and essay practice
Leaving Data Insights until last because it's unfamiliar. It's a third of the test
Using a calculator for Quant practice. You only get one in Data Insights
Judging progress by hours logged instead of by your accuracy and timing on practice sections

content.body: None of this needs you to quit your job or find hours that don't exist. It means being honest about the hours you have and using them well.
